intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an open-air sunrise yoga session overlooking the lush Campuhan valley, followed by a peaceful walk along the iconic ridge trail through tropical greenery. A perfect blend of mindfulness and nature immersion.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner-friendly surf lesson with a local instructor along the golden shores of Seminyak, then unwind on the beach to watch one of Bali's legendary sunsets with a fresh coconut in hand.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Bali's world-renowned wellness culture with daily yoga and meditation classes at The Yoga Barn, one of Asia's most celebrated retreat centers. Classes span Hatha, Vinyasa, and Yin styles.

experiences.name: Nusa Dua Snorkeling & Crystal Beach Day
experiences.description: Explore vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish on a guided snorkeling trip off the pristine shores of Nusa Dua, then relax on the calm, crystal-clear turquoise waters of one of Bali's most beautiful beaches.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Ubud Market Tour
experiences.description: Start with a guided tour of the vibrant Ubud traditional market to source fresh local ingredients, then learn to prepare authentic Balinese dishes like satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding with a local chef.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00. Take a pre-booked airport shuttle or shared Grab/Gojek ride to Aegean Bliss Resort (budget tip: avoid metered taxis at the airport). Check in, unpack, and freshen up. Take a short stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings and soak in the warm Bali sunshine.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the immediate beach area near the resort. Watch the sunset from the beach — one of Bali's most iconic free experiences. Browse the nearby local market stalls for souvenirs and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Warung (local eatery) near the resort — try Nasi Campur (mixed rice) for under IDR 30,000
meals.dinner: Local warung dinner near the beach — Mie Goreng or Nasi Goreng for IDR 25,000–40,000

day_by_day.notes: Download Gojek and Grab apps before arrival for cheap local transport. Exchange some currency at the airport kiosk or use a local ATM for better rates. Stay hydrated — warm summer weather expected at 25°C.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a free sunrise yoga session on the beach in front of the resort. Many beachfront areas in Bali have informal community yoga gatherings at dawn. Alternatively, find a budget yoga studio nearby offering drop-in classes for IDR 50,000–80,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (IDR 50,000–70,000/day) and explore the local coastal roads. Visit the nearest temple on the beach — most are free to enter with a sarong (available to borrow or rent at the entrance for IDR 10,000–15,000). Dip your toes in the warm ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local beachside night market or 'pasar malam' for cheap eats and atmosphere. Try fresh grilled corn, satay skewers, and tropical fruit.

meals.breakfast: Resort or nearby warung — Bubur Ayam (rice porridge) or banana pancakes for IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.lunch: Warung lunch — Gado-Gado (vegetable peanut salad) for IDR 25,000
meals.dinner: Night market street food — budget IDR 40,000–60,000 for a full spread

day_by_day.notes: Bring a sarong for temple visits — it is required and shows cultural respect. Apply sunscreen generously; UV index is high even on partly cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Join a morning yoga class at a local budget studio or beachside shala. Many studios in Bali offer donation-based or low-cost classes (IDR 50,000–100,000). Practice pranayama and sun salutations with an ocean view.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby popular beach known for good swimming and snorkeling. Rent snorkel gear for IDR 30,000–50,000 and explore the coral. Relax on the sand and enjoy the warm 25°C weather.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the beach promenade at sunset. Stop at a beachside warung for a Bintang beer (IDR 30,000) or fresh coconut (IDR 15,000) and enjoy the golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Local warung — Nasi Jinggo (small rice parcel) for IDR 5,000–10,000 each, grab 2–3
meals.lunch: Beach warung — grilled fish with rice and sambal for IDR 45,000–65,000
meals.dinner: Warung dinner — Ayam Betutu (slow-cooked chicken) with rice for IDR 40,000–55,000

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate snorkel gear rental prices — vendors often start high. Bring a reusable water bottle to save money and reduce plastic waste.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Gojek ride to a famous local temple or cultural landmark in the region (entry IDR 15,000–30,000). Spend the morning exploring the grounds, watching offerings being placed, and learning about Balinese Hindu traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a quieter, less-touristy beach nearby for an afternoon swim. Bring a packed lunch or stop at a small roadside warung. Enjoy the calm waves and warm water — perfect beach weather.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Take a leisurely evening walk and explore local shops. Try a traditional Balinese massage at a budget spa (IDR 80,000–120,000 for 60 minutes).

meals.breakfast: Resort area warung — fried rice with egg for IDR 25,000
meals.lunch: Roadside warung near the beach — Soto Ayam (chicken soup) for IDR 20,000–30,000
meals.dinner: Local restaurant — Babi Guling (suckling pig) or vegetarian equivalent for IDR 50,000–70,000

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting temples — shoulders and knees must be covered. Budget massage parlors are widely available and excellent value.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn beach yoga or meditation session on the sand — completely free and incredibly peaceful. Watch local fishermen head out to sea. Collect shells along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local traditional market (pasar tradisional). Browse fresh produce, spices, flowers, and handcrafts. This is a great place to buy affordable souvenirs like sarongs, incense, and woven baskets.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost Kecak fire dance performance if available nearby (IDR 50,000–100,000). These dramatic sunset performances are a highlight of any Bali trip.

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast — fresh tropical fruit plate and Jamu (herbal drink) for IDR 20,000
meals.lunch: Traditional market food stall — Lawar (Balinese mixed dish) for IDR 25,000–35,000
meals.dinner: Warung near the performance venue — Nasi Goreng Special for IDR 35,000

day_by_day.notes: Arrive early at the traditional market for the freshest produce and best atmosphere — most stalls open from 6:00 AM. Check local listings for Kecak performance schedules.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning yoga immersion — find a 2-hour budget yoga workshop or flow class at a local studio (IDR 80,000–150,000). Focus on deepening your practice in Bali's spiritual environment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the resort beach. Read, swim, and recharge. This is a rest afternoon — budget travel can be tiring, so pacing yourself is important. Enjoy the beachfront amenities.
day_by_day.evening: Cook your own simple meal or join a budget cooking class introduction. Alternatively, enjoy a cheap local dinner and then stargaze on the beach — Bali's skies can be spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl from a local café — IDR 35,000–50,000
meals.lunch: Resort area warung — Tempeh Goreng with rice for IDR 20,000–30,000
meals.dinner: Beachside warung — fresh grilled prawn skewers with rice for IDR 55,000–75,000

day_by_day.notes: Midway through the trip is a good time to do laundry at a local laundry service (IDR 15,000–20,000 per kg — very affordable). Rest days are important for long trips.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter (IDR 60,000–80,000/day) and explore the surrounding coastal villages. Stop at viewpoints and small fishing villages. Scooters are the most budget-friendly way to see Bali independently.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a hidden or less-crowded beach accessible by scooter. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying the scenery. Pack a simple picnic from a local warung.
day_by_day.evening: Return scooter and enjoy a relaxed evening near the resort. Browse beachside cafés and enjoy a fresh fruit juice while watching the sunset.

meals.breakfast: Warung breakfast — banana pancakes with honey for IDR 25,000
meals.lunch: Packed warung lunch — Nasi Bungkus (wrapped rice with sides) for IDR 20,000–30,000
meals.dinner: Local seafood warung — grilled fish with plecing kangkung (water spinach) for IDR 50,000–65,000

day_by_day.notes: Always wear a helmet when riding a scooter — it is the law and essential for safety. Carry your international driver's license. Fill up the tank at a Pertamina station or roadside fuel vendor.

day_by_day.morning: Morning beach walk at sunrise, followed by a free outdoor yoga or stretching session. Journal your Bali experiences so far. Reflect on the spiritual energy of the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local waterfall or rice terrace accessible by Gojek or scooter. Many natural attractions in Bali charge a small entry fee of IDR 10,000–20,000. Take photos and enjoy nature.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beach area. Enjoy a traditional Balinese foot massage (IDR 60,000–80,000 for 30 minutes). Wind down with herbal tea at a local café.

meals.breakfast: Local warung — Bubur Sumsum (rice flour porridge with coconut milk) for IDR 15,000
meals.lunch: Roadside warung near the natural attraction — Mie Goreng for IDR 25,000
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant — Nasi Campur platter with multiple sides for IDR 40,000–55,000

day_by_day.notes: Natural attractions can get busy by mid-morning — arrive early for the best experience and photos. Bring insect repellent for waterfall or jungle areas.

day_by_day.morning: Attend a longer yoga or meditation class — look for a half-day yoga retreat or workshop (IDR 150,000–250,000). Many budget-friendly spiritual centers in Bali offer immersive morning sessions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby coastal village on foot. Chat with locals, visit a small family-run temple, and observe daily Balinese life. This is a free and deeply enriching cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the beach for a bonfire gathering if available, or simply sit by the ocean and enjoy the sounds of the waves. Buy a cheap Bintang from a convenience store and relax.

meals.breakfast: Yoga center café — healthy smoothie and toast for IDR 40,000–55,000
meals.lunch: Village warung — home-cooked Balinese meal for IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.dinner: Beachfront warung — Ikan Bakar (grilled fish) with sambal and rice for IDR 50,000–70,000

day_by_day.notes: Ask your yoga instructor for recommendations on hidden local gems — they often know the best budget spots that tourists miss.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise surf lesson or bodyboard session on the beach (IDR 100,000–150,000 for a beginner lesson including board rental). Bali's warm water and gentle morning waves are perfect for beginners.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on the beach and dry off. Browse local art shops and craft stalls — practice your bargaining skills for the best prices. Look for handmade jewelry, paintings, and batik fabric.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate being 10 days into your trip. Find a mid-range restaurant with a beach view that still fits the budget.

meals.breakfast: Pre-surf warung breakfast — Nasi Goreng with fried egg for IDR 25,000
meals.lunch: Beach café — fresh coconut and a light snack for IDR 30,000
meals.dinner: Slightly upgraded warung or local restaurant — seafood platter for IDR 80,000–120,000 (a small treat)

day_by_day.notes: Surfing is a quintessential Bali experience even for beginners. Morning sessions have calmer winds and smaller crowds. Always negotiate art and souvenir prices — starting at half the asking price is standard.

day_by_day.morning: Final dedicated yoga morning — practice on the beach independently using everything you have learned during the trip. Bring a mat (borrow from the resort or studio) and face the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore any remaining local sights you have not yet visited — a nearby temple, viewpoint, or beach. Use this afternoon to revisit your favorite spot from the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cultural event, community gathering, or temple ceremony if one is happening nearby. Balinese ceremonies are frequent and visitors are often welcome to observe respectfully.

meals.breakfast: Local warung — fresh fruit platter and Jamu shot for IDR 25,000
meals.lunch: Favorite warung from earlier in the trip — revisit a meal you loved
meals.dinner: Night market dinner — variety of street food for IDR 50,000–70,000 total

day_by_day.notes: Start thinking about any last-minute souvenirs or gifts to buy tomorrow. Check your flight details and confirm your departure transport arrangements.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk and meditation. Take photos and video to capture memories. Swim one last time in the warm Bali ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at local markets. Buy spices, Balinese coffee, essential oils, or handmade crafts as gifts. Pack any fragile items carefully.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — choose your favorite local warung or beachside spot from the trip. Reflect on the incredible 13-day journey over a final Bali meal.

meals.breakfast: Resort area warung — full Balinese breakfast spread for IDR 35,000–45,000
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach café — Gado-Gado salad for IDR 30,000
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your favorite warung — budget IDR 60,000–80,000 for a memorable last meal

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing tonight. Weigh your luggage to avoid airline excess baggage fees. Set an alarm and confirm your departure time and transport to the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali — wake up early for one last sunrise if your departure allows. Enjoy a quiet breakfast and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage at reception if needed for a late checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, spend remaining hours at the nearest beach or simply relax at the resort. Book your Grab or Gojek ride to Ngurah Rai International Airport in advance to avoid last-minute stress.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali with incredible memories of beaches, yoga, culture, and budget-friendly adventure. Carry the island's spiritual energy with you.

meals.breakfast: Final warung breakfast — Nasi Goreng or banana pancakes for IDR 25,000–35,000
meals.lunch: Airport food court or pack a final warung meal to eat before departure — IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: On the flight or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Declare any food items (spices, coffee) at customs if required. Keep some IDR cash for airport taxes or last-minute purchases — departure tax is usually included in the ticket price but confirm in advance.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Bali (Flight LH lands at 13:00) — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Ngurah Rai International Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort (~45–60 min depending on traffic). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room. Take a leisurely stroll along the beach in front of the resort to get your bearings and enjoy the warm afternoon sun.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the resort beach or nearby beach bar. Explore the immediate beachfront strip and enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a casual warung near the resort upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant — try local staples like Nasi Goreng or Mie Goreng (mid-range, ~$10–15 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — rest and acclimatize. Exchange some currency at the airport for convenience. Average high 25°C; light layers for the evening are handy.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a sunrise beach yoga session — either through the resort's yoga program or a nearby beachfront yoga studio. A 60–75 min Hatha or Vinyasa class facing the ocean sets a wonderful tone for the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby iconic beach (such as Seminyak or Kuta Beach if staying in that area) for swimming, sunbathing, and people-watching. Rent a sun lounger (~$5) and enjoy the warm water.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local area on foot. Visit a beach club for sunset cocktails, then head to a nearby street-side warung for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a local café — avocado toast, tropical fruit platter, and Bali coffee (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Beachside café lunch — grilled fish, fresh coconut water, and a salad (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a local warung — Babi Guling (suckling pig) or Lawar with steamed rice (~$7–10)

day_by_day.notes: Apply sunscreen generously — even on cloudy days UV index is high in Bali. Carry a reusable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga class at a dedicated yoga studio — look for a Yin Yoga or Pranayama session (~$10–15). Follow with a healthy smoothie bowl breakfast nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local temple in the area (such as Tanah Lot if in the Seminyak/Canggu area, or Uluwatu if in the south). Hire a local driver for a half-day (~$20–25). Dress respectfully with a sarong (available to rent at the temple).
day_by_day.evening: If visiting Uluwatu, catch the famous Kecak Fire Dance performance at sunset (~$15 entry). Return to the resort area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl and cold brew at a trendy café near the yoga studio (~$6–9)
meals.lunch: Warungs near the temple — Nasi Campur (mixed rice plate) (~$4–7)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant dinner — grilled seafood platter with local sambal and vegetables (~$15–20)

day_by_day.notes: Kecak Dance at Uluwatu is a must-see cultural experience. Book tickets slightly in advance during peak season. Bring a light jacket for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning — wake up early for a swim before crowds arrive. Try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) or snorkeling if available near the resort (~$15–20 rental). The calm morning water is ideal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a cooking class in the local area (many resorts or nearby venues offer 3-hour Balinese cooking classes, ~$30–40). Learn to make dishes like Satay, Lawar, and Jamu (herbal drink).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the meal you cooked! Or head out to a night market (pasar malam) for local street food and atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort — fresh fruit, yogurt, and local coffee (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Eat what you prepare in the cooking class (included in most class fees)
meals.dinner: Night market street food — satay skewers, martabak (stuffed pancake), fresh juices (~$5–8)

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes are a fantastic mid-range activity that combines culture, food, and fun. Book the previous day to secure a spot.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ubud — hire a driver for the day (~$35–45 round trip). Start with the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary (Mandala Suci Wenara Wana) — a lush jungle sanctuary with ancient temples and resident macaques (~$5 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Ubud's central market (Pasar Ubud) for souvenirs, textiles, and local crafts. Visit the Ubud Royal Palace (Puri Saren Agung) — free entry. Browse Ubud's main street for art galleries and boutique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Balinese dance performance in Ubud (Legong or Barong dance, ~$10–12). Dinner in Ubud before the drive back.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a popular Ubud café — try Locavore To Go or a similar farm-to-table spot (~$10–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ubud — Bebek Betutu (slow-cooked duck) at a traditional Balinese restaurant (~$12–18)

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is approximately 1–1.5 hours from the coast. Secure valuables around the monkeys at the Monkey Forest — they are known to snatch items. Bring cash as many small vendors don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Yoga and wellness morning — attend a 90-minute Vinyasa Flow or Ashtanga class at the resort or a nearby studio. Follow with a traditional Balinese massage (~$15–25 for 60 min at a local spa).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the beach or resort pool. Read, journal, or simply decompress. This is a designated rest afternoon to recharge mid-trip.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the beach. Enjoy a quiet dinner at a beachside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort — eggs, tropical fruits, toast, and Balinese coffee (~$8–12)
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — club sandwich or Caesar salad (~$8–10)
meals.dinner: Romantic beachside dinner — grilled lobster or fish with local sides (~$18–25)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest days are essential for a balanced itinerary. The Balinese massage (pijat Bali) uses a combination of acupressure, reflexology, and aromatherapy — deeply relaxing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tegalalang Rice Terraces (day trip from the coast, ~1.5 hrs). Arrive early (~8:00 AM) to beat crowds and enjoy the cool morning mist over the iconic UNESCO-listed terraced fields. Walk the trails and take in panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the way back, stop at a local coffee plantation for a Kopi Luwak (civet coffee) tasting experience (~$5–10). Visit a traditional silver or batik workshop in the Celuk or Batubulan area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a sundowner at a beach club and a casual dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a café overlooking the rice terraces — Nasi Goreng or fresh spring rolls (~$7–10)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a beach club — burgers, tacos, or local dishes (~$12–16)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the rice terrace trails. Some sections have steep steps. A small entrance fee (~$2) may be charged by local farmers maintaining the area. Bring a hat and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Water sports morning at the beach — try surfing with a beginner lesson if you haven't surfed before (~$25–35 including board and instructor, 2 hours). Bali's waves are excellent for beginners in certain spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby Hindu temple or cultural site. If in the Uluwatu area, explore the clifftop paths. If near Seminyak/Canggu, visit Pura Petitenget temple — a significant sea temple with beautiful architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a local night market or the Seminyak/Canggu strip for dinner and drinks. Enjoy the vibrant Bali nightlife at a moderate pace.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the surf school — acai bowl, granola, or eggs (~$6–9)
meals.lunch: Post-surf lunch at a beachside warung — Nasi Campur or grilled corn (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant — wood-fired pizza, pasta, or Asian fusion (~$12–18)

day_by_day.notes: Surfing lessons are widely available along Kuta, Seminyak, and Canggu beaches. Beginners should always use a foam board and stay in designated beginner zones.

day_by_day.morning: Morning meditation and pranayama (breathwork) session — either through the resort program or a dedicated meditation center nearby (~$10–15). Follow with a healthy breakfast and journaling time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore local boutique shopping — Bali is famous for handmade goods, linen clothing, rattan bags, and artisan jewelry. Browse local boutiques in the Seminyak/Canggu/Ubud area depending on your base. Budget ~$30–50 for souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at a famous viewpoint or beach club. Enjoy live acoustic music (many beach clubs host live sets at sunset). Dinner at a rooftop restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Healthy café breakfast — smoothie bowl, chia pudding, or granola with tropical fruit (~$6–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café — avocado toast, salad bowl, or bao buns (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant dinner — panoramic views with Indonesian or international cuisine (~$15–22)

day_by_day.notes: Bali's boutique shopping is excellent value. Bargaining is expected at markets but not in boutique stores. Always carry small bills (IDR) for market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day trip to the Nusa Penida or Nusa Lembongan islands (ferry from Sanur, ~45 min, ~$15–20 round trip). Morning: arrive and explore the stunning cliffs and beaches — visit Kelingking Beach viewpoint (dramatic T-Rex shaped cliff) and Crystal Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling trip around Nusa Penida — the waters are home to manta rays, colorful coral reefs, and diverse marine life. Guided snorkeling tours available on the island (~$20–30 including equipment).
day_by_day.evening: Ferry back to Bali. Arrive at Sanur and transfer back to the resort. Quiet dinner near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before heading to Sanur ferry terminal
meals.lunch: Lunch on Nusa Penida — fresh grilled fish, coconut rice, and cold drinks at a local warung (~$6–10)
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner near the resort — soup, salad, and a local dish (~$10–14)

day_by_day.notes: The ferry to Nusa Penida departs from Sanur Beach (~30–40 min drive from Seminyak). Book ferry tickets in advance during peak season. The island roads are rugged — hire a local driver/scooter on the island. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga on the beach — a special outdoor session at the water's edge. Many resorts and local instructors offer this as a premium experience. Alternatively, practice independently on the beach at dawn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a Balinese healer (Balian) or participate in a traditional purification ritual at a local water temple such as Tirta Empul (holy spring temple near Ubud, ~1.5 hrs). This is a spiritually profound cultural experience (~$5–10 entry + sarong rental).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Treat yourself to a full-body spa treatment — traditional Boreh body scrub and floral bath (~$30–45 at a local spa). Light dinner.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga breakfast at the resort — full spread with local options (~$8–12)
meals.lunch: Lunch near Tirta Empul — Nasi Goreng and fresh juice at a local warung (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Light and healthy dinner — grilled vegetables, tofu satay, and herbal tea (~$8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Tirta Empul is one of Bali's most sacred temples. Visitors are welcome to participate in the melukat (purification bathing ritual) with respect. Wear a sarong and act reverently. Avoid visiting during menstruation as per local customs.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — swim, snorkel, or simply lounge on the beachfront. Soak in the last days of sun and sea. Try a fresh coconut on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping and packing. Visit a local spa for a final Balinese massage or reflexology session (~$15–25). Pick up any last items — local spices, Bali coffee, sarongs, or artwork.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special restaurant — splurge slightly for the last night. Choose a restaurant with an ocean view or a well-regarded local fine dining spot.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort — enjoy the full spread one last time (~$8–12)
meals.lunch: Casual beach lunch — fish tacos, fresh fruit, and a cold drink (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner — premium Balinese seafood feast or tasting menu at a top local restaurant (~$25–40)

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight. Keep travel documents, passport, and boarding pass easily accessible. Check flight time for Day 13 and arrange airport transfer in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk or short beach meditation. Check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort. Transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport (allow at least 2–3 hours before departure for international flights).
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Bali. Spend any remaining IDR at the airport on last-minute snacks, Bali coffee, or duty-free items.
day_by_day.evening: In transit or at destination — reflect on 13 wonderful days in Bali.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or airport café — keep it light for travel (~$5–10)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café lunch before boarding
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Bali's airport can be busy — arrive early. Confirm your flight status the night before. Consider downloading offline maps and keeping a copy of your hotel receipt for customs if required. Selamat jalan — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00. Private luxury transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort, Bali. Check in, unwind with a welcome drink and resort orientation. Explore the beachfront property, settle into your suite, and take a refreshing dip in the infinity pool overlooking the ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the private beach. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's signature beachfront restaurant, savoring fresh seafood and Indonesian specialties under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light snack or room service upon arrival
meals.dinner: Beachfront signature restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh grilled lobster, local sambal, and tropical desserts paired with a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in in advance if possible. Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Keep the first evening light to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach yoga session on the private resort beach with a certified instructor. Follow with a nourishing breakfast at the resort's ocean-view terrace. Take a leisurely morning swim in the warm Indian Ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided snorkeling excursion along the nearby coral reef. Explore vibrant marine life in the crystal-clear waters off the Bali coast. Return to the resort for a luxurious spa treatment — opt for the traditional Balinese massage with aromatic oils.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktail hour at the resort's rooftop bar watching the golden sunset. Dinner at a premium local restaurant nearby featuring authentic Balinese rijsttafel (rice table) cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit platter, Nasi Goreng, fresh-pressed juices, and Balinese coffee at the ocean terrace
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled fish tacos, açaí bowls, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Upscale Balinese rijsttafel at a renowned nearby restaurant — multiple small dishes including satay, rendang, and tempeh with premium local Arak cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book the spa treatment in advance as slots fill quickly. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. Yoga session begins at 06:30 — confirm with resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga and pranayama breathwork session on the beach. Meditation overlooking the ocean as the sun rises. Followed by a healthy smoothie bowl breakfast at the resort wellness café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private day trip to Tanah Lot Temple — one of Bali's most iconic sea temples perched on a rocky outcrop. Explore the temple grounds with a knowledgeable private guide learning about Balinese Hindu culture and history. Browse artisan craft stalls nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail. Enjoy a private candlelit dinner on the beach — a bespoke menu prepared by the resort's executive chef, featuring locally sourced ingredients and premium wines.

meals.breakfast: Wellness smoothie bowls, overnight oats, and herbal teas at the resort wellness café
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort chef enjoyed near Tanah Lot — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private candlelit beach dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — five-course tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is approximately 20 km from most beachfront resorts — private car transfer recommended. Wear a sarong at the temple (available for rent on-site). Best visited in the afternoon for the iconic sunset backdrop.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga flow class at the resort's open-air yoga pavilion. Post-yoga, enjoy a full resort breakfast. Take a peaceful walk along the beach collecting shells and breathing in the ocean air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private surf lesson with a professional instructor on the nearby beach break — ideal for all skill levels. Spend time relaxing on a luxury sunbed with personalized beach butler service, chilled towels, and fresh fruit.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a nearby upscale beach club for sundowners — enjoy premium cocktails, DJ music, and ocean views. Dinner at the beach club's fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet — eggs benedict, tropical fruits, freshly baked pastries, and Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Beach butler service — fresh ceviche, grilled prawns, and chilled coconut water served on the sunbed
meals.dinner: Premium beach club restaurant — Wagyu beef sliders, tuna tartare, and lobster bisque with craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Surf lessons are suitable for beginners — confirm level with instructor. Apply high SPF sunscreen before surf lesson. Beach club reservations recommended for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided meditation and yoga nidra (yogic sleep) session on the beach at sunrise. Followed by a nutritious breakfast. Visit the resort's wellness center for a private consultation on Ayurvedic wellness practices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private day excursion to Uluwatu Temple — a dramatic clifftop sea temple offering breathtaking panoramic views of the Indian Ocean. Explore the surrounding limestone cliffs and watch local monkeys in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the legendary Kecak Fire Dance performance at Uluwatu at sunset — a spectacular traditional Balinese dance performed against the backdrop of the setting sun. Dinner at a cliffside fine dining restaurant in Uluwatu.

meals.breakfast: Açaí bowls, avocado toast, poached eggs, and fresh juices at the resort
meals.lunch: Cliffside café near Uluwatu — grilled fish, local vegetables, and fresh lime juice
meals.dinner: Upscale cliffside restaurant in Uluwatu — Indonesian seafood platter, prawn satay, and black rice pudding dessert with ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Kecak Dance tickets should be booked in advance. Wear a sarong at Uluwatu Temple. Keep belongings secure around the monkeys. Private transfer recommended — approximately 30–45 minutes from the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning — sleep in or enjoy a gentle beach walk. Late breakfast at the resort. Book a full-day luxury spa package beginning mid-morning — traditional Balinese massage, body scrub, floral bath, and facial.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue spa treatments or relax by the infinity pool with a good book. Enjoy a light poolside lunch. Optional: private painting or Balinese craft workshop at the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic sunset cruise along the Bali coastline on a private chartered catamaran. Enjoy champagne, canapés, and panoramic views of the coastline as the sun dips below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely à la carte breakfast at the resort — French toast with tropical compote, fresh juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside light lunch — Caesar salad, prawn skewers, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Dinner served on the private sunset catamaran — champagne, gourmet canapés, charcuterie boards, and fresh seafood

day_by_day.notes: Full spa day is a perfect mid-trip recovery day. Catamaran sunset cruise must be booked 48 hours in advance. Bring a light wrap for the evening sea breeze on the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga on the beach followed by breakfast. Private driver day trip to Ubud — Bali's cultural and artistic heartland. Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary for a walk among ancient temples and playful long-tailed macaques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's famous art market for premium Balinese handicrafts, textiles, and jewelry. Visit the Agung Rai Museum of Art (ARMA) for a curated collection of traditional and contemporary Balinese artwork. Stroll through the royal Ubud Palace.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Ubud at one of the region's finest farm-to-table restaurants set amidst lush rice paddies. Return to the resort by private car.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Balinese porridge, tropical fruits, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Ubud organic café — locally grown vegetable dishes, tempeh, and fresh herbal juices
meals.dinner: Premium farm-to-table restaurant in Ubud — slow-cooked Balinese duck (bebek betutu), organic vegetables, and artisan desserts in a stunning rice paddy setting

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is approximately 1–1.5 hours from the beachfront resort by private car. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Monkey Forest. Keep bags secure around monkeys. Book the Ubud dinner restaurant in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga and breathwork session at the resort. Breakfast followed by a private guided beach walk exploring the local coastline, tide pools, and hidden coves inaccessible to the general public.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon paddleboarding or kayaking along the calm coastal waters. Followed by a relaxing session in the resort's hydrotherapy pool and steam room. Optional: book a private sound healing meditation session.
day_by_day.evening: Dress for a premium dinner experience at one of Bali's most acclaimed fine dining restaurants — a tasting menu showcasing modern Indonesian cuisine with international techniques.

meals.breakfast: Healthy resort breakfast — granola, Greek yogurt, fresh berries, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light resort lunch by the pool — sashimi platter, miso soup, and edamame
meals.dinner: Acclaimed fine dining restaurant — modern Indonesian tasting menu (8 courses) with wine pairing, featuring local spices and premium imported ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Sound healing session should be booked with the resort wellness team. Fine dining dinner reservation is essential — book at least 3 days in advance. Smart casual dress code for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga session followed by a visit to a nearby Balinese Hindu temple for a private blessing ceremony with a local priest — a deeply spiritual and authentic cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class with a renowned local chef — learn to prepare traditional Balinese dishes including satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding using fresh market ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class as a private dinner experience. Alternatively, head to a rooftop restaurant for panoramic sunset views and a celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — eggs your way, smoked salmon, and Balinese black rice porridge
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes prepared during your cooking class — a rewarding and authentic experience
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant with panoramic ocean views — grilled whole fish, lobster thermidor, and tropical sorbet with premium cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Temple blessing ceremony requires modest clothing — sarong and sash provided. Cooking class typically lasts 3–4 hours including a market visit. Confirm cooking class booking 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a luxurious in-room breakfast. Late morning beach yoga or self-guided stretching on your private balcony. Spend time journaling or reading by the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chartered speedboat to a secluded nearby island or sandbar for an exclusive beach picnic experience. Snorkel in pristine waters, sunbathe on untouched white sand, and enjoy total seclusion.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail. Dinner at the resort's premium beachfront restaurant — a special chef's table experience with personalized menu.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious in-room breakfast — eggs benedict, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, champagne, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet private island picnic — chilled seafood, artisan cheeses, fresh baguettes, tropical fruits, and premium wines
meals.dinner: Chef's table experience at the resort — personalized 6-course menu crafted to your preferences with sommelier wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Private island speedboat excursion must be arranged through the resort concierge at least 2 days in advance. Chef's table is a premium add-on — confirm with the resort. Perfect day for photography — bring a waterproof camera.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga and meditation on the beach. Breakfast at the resort. Private guided visit to Pura Luhur Batukaru — one of Bali's most sacred and serene mountain temples surrounded by lush jungle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jatiluwih UNESCO Rice Terraces — stunning emerald-green terraced rice fields offering breathtaking views. Walk along the terrace pathways with a private guide learning about traditional Balinese subak irrigation systems.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a couples' or solo massage. Dinner at a premium restaurant with live traditional Balinese gamelan music.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoothie bowls, avocado toast, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Local warung near Jatiluwih — traditional Nasi Campur (mixed rice) with locally grown organic vegetables
meals.dinner: Premium restaurant with live gamelan music — Balinese spiced duck, grilled barramundi, and coconut panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Jatiluwih and Batukaru are approximately 1.5–2 hours from the resort — start early. Bring comfortable walking shoes and insect repellent for the rice terrace walk. A light rain jacket is advisable.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning yoga session — a reflective and restorative practice on the beach. Followed by a special wellness breakfast. Visit the resort spa for a final indulgent treatment — hot stone massage or deep tissue session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure afternoon — enjoy the resort's amenities one last time: infinity pool, private beach, and ocean views. Optional last-minute souvenir shopping at nearby premium boutiques for Balinese jewelry, textiles, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's most exclusive dining venue — a premium multi-course celebration of Balinese flavors and international cuisine. Toast to an unforgettable trip with a bottle of fine champagne.

meals.breakfast: Special wellness breakfast — detox juices, superfood bowls, and herbal elixirs at the wellness café
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — mezze platter, grilled halloumi, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's exclusive restaurant — premium multi-course Balinese and international menu with champagne and fine wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Pack non-essential luggage in the evening to ease departure preparation. Request a late checkout if your flight allows. Purchase any last souvenirs or gifts from the resort boutique.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk or a short gentle yoga practice. Enjoy a last leisurely breakfast at the resort savoring the ocean views. Complete packing and checkout formalities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — optional last swim, spa visit, or poolside relaxation. Private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Allow 2.5–3 hours before departure for international check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of beaches, yoga, culture, and luxury as you board your flight home.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — a full spread of favorites enjoyed slowly with ocean views
meals.lunch: Light airport lounge dining or an early lunch at the resort before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time and private airport transfer with the resort concierge the evening before. Keep valuables and travel documents in your carry-on. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Enjoy the journey home with beautiful memories of Bali.

query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA
